English.Text: Diwan Intrigues — The Speech
At last, the Diwan of Wadi Al Zahir has granted me a seat! My inaugural speech must be flawless — the Grand Vizier reads every report from the provinces.
It is done. If the Diwan is not moved by this, they have hearts of stone. Thank you, Governor.
Are you mad? Half of them were born here! You want me to tell them I am counting the days until I can leave?
Envoy Kemal Bey has been given a seat in the city's Diwan and wants your help with his inaugural speech.
Kemal Bey: 'They say that in the Diwan, the first words decide everything. I shall rise, bow to the chair and address them as "Esteemed brothers of the Diwan"... and then? How should I begin?'

Kemal Bey was once a promising secretary at the Sultan's court, until an unfortunate incident involving a cup of coffee and the Grand Vizier's finest kaftan saw him posted to the furthest corner of the Sultanate. A seat in the provincial Diwan is his first step back to the capital, and his inaugural speech must make an impression that travels all the way there.
Kemal Bey: 'Good. Now the substance — what my first mandate shall be. The Grand Vizier will read this, remember. What should I promise them?'
Kemal Bey: 'And the closing words... they must be remembered. Something worthy of being quoted in the capital. How should I end?'
'...I am humbled that you have finally taken notice of me...'
'...together, we shall make this province the envy of the capital...'
'...after many years of patient service, I stand before you at last...'
'...to lighten the burdens of the Nomads, whose labour feeds this province...'
'...to extend the reach of our mosques, so that no quarter is beyond the call to prayer...'
'...to make life in Wadi Al Zahir worthy of the Sultan's servants...'
'...may the Diwan of Wadi Al Zahir one day be spoken of in the same breath as the Diwan of the capital!'
'...I shall serve this Diwan as faithfully as I once served the Sultan's own household!'
'...I shall not rest until I am recalled to the capital and never have to see this dusty province again!'
Kemal Bey thanks you for your help with his speech.
Kemal Bey is not amused — even if the suggestion was uncomfortably close to the truth.
